TRIAGE (Earth System Trend Intelligence & Impact Explorer) is an interactive platform designed to help users discover, analyse, and understand significant changes in Earth's interconnected environmental systems.

The platform brings together NASA Earth science datasets, regional time-series visualisation, geospatial exploration, and statistical trend analysis. It aims to identify what is changing, where it is changing, how rapidly it is changing, and whether those changes are statistically significant using methods such as the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope.

Our initial implementation focuses on historical MERRA-2 precipitation data, covering 2001–2025, with plans to incorporate additional datasets such as GPM IMERG, GLDAS, and MODIS. An AI-powered scientific assistant will help users interpret analytical results, explore relationships between environmental variables, and understand regional implications.

By making complex Earth science data more accessible and interpretable, TRIAGE aims to turn users into Earth System Trend Detectives and support data-driven environmental understanding.
details:
TRIAGE — Earth System Trend Intelligence & Impact Explorer

TRIAGE is an interactive platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, designed to help users investigate and understand changes in Earth's environmental systems through data-driven trend analysis.

The platform aims to answer four important questions: What is changing? Where is it changing? How fast is it changing? And is the observed change statistically significant?

Our initial implementation focuses on historical NASA MERRA-2 precipitation data (PRECTOTCORR), covering 2001–2025 at monthly resolution for a selected region in northern India. Users can explore environmental time series, visualize historical patterns, and apply statistical methods such as the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope to investigate trend direction, magnitude, and significance. Confidence intervals and considerations such as seasonality and temporal autocorrelation can further support reliable interpretation.

TRIAGE also incorporates the concept of an AI-powered Earth Detective assistant to make scientific findings easier to understand. Rather than replacing scientific analysis, the assistant is intended to explain computed results in accessible language and help users explore environmental relationships.

The project aims to make complex Earth observation data more accessible to students, researchers, and environmental enthusiasts. Its longer-term vision is to bring multiple environmental variables together, including precipitation, soil moisture, land surface temperature, and vegetation indicators, helping users investigate interconnected Earth system changes.

We developed the project using modern web development and data-processing technologies, including Python for backend data handling and statistical analysis, and JavaScript/TypeScript-based web technologies for the interactive interface. The platform follows a modular architecture to support future dataset integrations and analytical capabilities.

The creative aspect of TRIAGE is its combination of Earth observation data, statistical trend detection, interactive visualization, and AI-assisted scientific interpretation in one exploration workflow. Instead of merely displaying environmental measurements, it helps users investigate the meaning behind them.

During development, our team considered scientific reliability, data availability, regional relevance, usability, interpretability, scalability, and the importance of distinguishing statistically significant trends from ordinary fluctuations. We also considered the limitations of historical datasets and the need to avoid presenting correlation as causation.

Our vision is to turn complex environmental data into understandable scientific insights and empower more people to become Earth System Trend Detectives.
